questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal $(X)$ dissolves both in dilute $\mathrm{HCl}$ and dilute $\mathrm{NaOH}$ to liberate $\mathrm{H}_{2}$. Addition of $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ and excess $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ to an HCl solution of $\mathrm{X}$ produce $\mathrm{Y}$ as a precipitate. $\mathrm{Y}$ is also produced by adding $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ to $\mathrm{t}$ he $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution of $\mathrm{X}$. The species $\mathrm{X}$ and $Y$, respectively, are
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{ZnO}_{2} \mathrm{Al}+\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaClO}_{2}\\
\mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnCl}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{Al}+\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{AlCl}_{3}+\mathrm{H}_{2}
\end{array}\mathrm{ZnCl}_{2}$ gives no ppt with $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ solution.
But $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ gives gelatinious white $\mathrm{ppt}$ of $\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ with $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$.
